chapters.title: Unity in Christ and the wisdom of the cross

parts.text: Paul greets the Corinthian church and thanks God for the grace and gifts given through Christ. Reports of factions around Paul, Apollos, Cephas, and Christ lead him to plead for unity. Christ is not divided, and Paul was neither crucified for them nor the name into which they were baptized. His commission is to preach the gospel without eloquence that empties the cross of its power.

The cross seems foolish to those perishing but is God’s saving power. Neither Jewish demands for signs nor Greek quests for wisdom determine Paul’s message: he preaches Christ crucified. God chooses the weak and despised to overturn human boasting. Christ becomes believers’ wisdom, righteousness, sanctification, and redemption, so their glory belongs in the Lord.

chapters.title: God’s wisdom is revealed by his Spirit

parts.text: Paul recalls coming in weakness and fear, determined to proclaim Jesus Christ crucified rather than impress through human eloquence. His preaching demonstrated the Spirit and power so that the Corinthians’ faith would rest on God rather than human wisdom.

He nevertheless speaks wisdom among the mature: God’s formerly hidden wisdom, ordained before the world for their glory. The rulers did not understand it, or they would not have crucified the Lord of glory. God reveals his prepared gifts through the Spirit, who searches even his deep things. The Spirit teaches their words and enables spiritual discernment. The natural man rejects these things as foolishness, while believers have the mind of Christ.

chapters.title: God’s servants, Christ’s foundation, and tested work

parts.text: Jealousy and faction show the Corinthians’ immaturity. Paul and Apollos are servants through whom they believed, not rival masters. One plants and another waters, but God gives growth. Each worker will receive a reward for his labour, and the church is God’s field and building.

Paul laid the foundation, Jesus Christ, and others must build carefully upon it. Fire will reveal the quality of each person’s work: lasting work receives reward, while burned work brings loss, though the worker is saved. The church is God’s holy temple, indwelt by his Spirit, and defiling it brings judgment. Human wisdom and boasting must give way to belonging to Christ, through whom all things are theirs.

chapters.title: Faithful stewards and an apostle’s fatherly warning

parts.text: Apostles should be regarded as Christ’s servants and faithful stewards of God’s mysteries. Final judgment belongs to the Lord, who will expose hidden motives at his coming. Everything the Corinthians possess was received, leaving no ground for pride. Paul contrasts their self-satisfaction with the apostles’ hunger, insecurity, labour, persecution, and patient blessing of those who abuse them.

He writes as a father warning beloved children, having begotten them through the gospel, and asks them to follow his example. Timotheus will remind them of Paul’s ways in Christ, taught consistently in the churches. Paul intends to visit if the Lord wills and test arrogant people’s power, not merely their speech. Their response will determine whether he comes with correction or gentleness.

chapters.title: Remove corrupting sin from the church

parts.text: Paul rebukes the church for pride instead of mourning over a man’s sexual relationship with his father’s wife. He directs the assembled believers, in the Lord Jesus’ name and power, to deliver the offender to Satan for destruction of the flesh so his spirit may be saved in the Lord’s day. Like leaven spreading through dough, tolerated wickedness affects the whole. Christ their passover has been sacrificed, calling them to sincerity and truth.

Paul clarifies that separation from immoral people does not mean abandoning all contact with the world. The discipline concerns someone called a brother who persists in listed evils. They must not keep company or eat with such a person. God judges outsiders; the church must put away the wicked person within.

chapters.title: Settle disputes rightly and honour God with the body

parts.text: Paul condemns believers taking their disputes before unbelieving courts rather than seeking judgment among saints, who will judge the world and angels. Accepting wrong would be better than defrauding one another. He warns that the unrighteous will not inherit God’s kingdom, listing sexual sins, idolatry, theft, greed, drunkenness, and other abuses. Some Corinthians once lived so, but have been washed, sanctified, and justified through Christ and God’s Spirit.

Liberty does not make everything beneficial or justify being mastered by anything. The body belongs to the Lord and will be raised by his power. Joining Christ’s members to a harlot is intolerable. Believers must flee fornication and glorify God in body and spirit: bought with a price, they are the Holy Ghost’s temple.

Paul addresses questions about marriage, urging mutual marital obligations and allowing temporary abstinence only by agreement for fasting and prayer. Singleness is good, but marriage is appropriate where self-control is lacking. Married believers should not separate; believers with willing unbelieving spouses should remain together, though a departing unbeliever may leave. Paul distinguishes the Lord’s command from his own instruction and urges faithful service within one’s calling.

Because of the present distress and passing world, he counsels remaining unmarried while affirming that marriage is no sin. Singleness can allow attention to the Lord without divided concerns. His advice seeks their good, not a trap. He discusses giving a virgin in marriage and permits a widow to remarry only in the Lord, while judging continued singleness happier.

chapters.title: Love limits liberty over food offered to idols

parts.text: Concerning food offered to idols, Paul contrasts knowledge that inflates pride with love that builds others up. An idol is nothing, and there is one God, the Father, from whom all things come, and one Lord Jesus Christ, through whom they exist. Yet merely claiming knowledge does not mean a person understands as he should.

Not every believer can eat such food without a troubled conscience. Food itself does not improve one’s standing with God, but careless liberty can encourage a weaker brother to violate conscience. Wounding a brother for whom Christ died is sin against Christ. Paul would rather give up meat altogether than cause his brother to stumble.

chapters.title: Paul relinquishes his rights for the gospel

parts.text: Paul defends his apostleship and the right of gospel workers to material support. Soldiers, farmers, shepherds, temple servants, and the law about an unmuzzled ox illustrate that workers share in their labour’s fruit. Yet he has declined support from the Corinthians rather than hinder the gospel. His entrusted commission compels him to preach, and he values offering it without charge.

Though free, he makes himself a servant to all, adapting to Jews, Gentiles, and the weak to gain them, while remaining under Christ’s law. He compares the Christian course to athletes training for a prize. Unlike a fading crown, their goal is incorruptible. Paul disciplines his body lest, after preaching to others, he himself become a castaway.

chapters.title: Learn from Israel and flee idolatry

parts.text: Israel shared the cloud, sea passage, and spiritual food and drink, with Christ identified as the spiritual Rock. Yet many fell in the wilderness. Their idolatry, fornication, tempting Christ, and murmuring warn believers against confident carelessness. Temptation is common to humanity, and God faithfully provides a way to endure it rather than allowing it beyond their ability.

Paul commands flight from idolatry. Participation in the Lord’s cup and bread is incompatible with fellowship at the table of devils. Liberty must serve another person’s good. Food sold in the market or served by an unbelieving host may be eaten without inquiry, but identified idol offerings should be declined for another’s conscience. Everything should glorify God and avoid needless offence, seeking others’ salvation.

chapters.title: Order in worship and reverence at the Lord’s supper

parts.text: Paul urges imitation of him as he follows Christ and discusses headship in prayer and prophecy. Men are not to pray or prophesy with covered heads, while women are to be covered. He relates these instructions to creation and honour while affirming man and woman’s interdependence in the Lord. The discussion also addresses hair and the churches’ practice.

He then rebukes divisions and selfish eating that leave some hungry and others drunk when the church gathers. Recounting Jesus’ institution of the bread and cup, he says the supper proclaims the Lord’s death until he comes. Participants must examine themselves and discern the Lord’s body. Irreverent participation has brought weakness, sickness, and death. They should wait for one another and satisfy ordinary hunger at home.

chapters.title: Many gifts and members, one Spirit and body

parts.text: Paul explains spiritual gifts by their relation to the Holy Ghost and confession of Jesus as Lord. Gifts, ministries, and workings differ, but come from the same Spirit, Lord, and God. Wisdom, knowledge, faith, healing, miracles, prophecy, discernment, tongues, and interpretation are distributed by the Spirit as he wills for the common benefit.

Believers, whether Jew or Gentile, bond or free, are baptized by one Spirit into one body. Like bodily members, none can deny belonging or dismiss another as unnecessary. God gives particular honour where needed so the members share suffering and joy without division. The church has various appointed functions, not identical gifts in everyone. Paul urges desire for the best gifts and introduces a more excellent way.

chapters.title: Charity is greater than gifts and remains

parts.text: Even extraordinary tongues, prophecy, knowledge, mountain-moving faith, generous giving, and bodily sacrifice profit nothing without charity. Charity is patient and kind rather than envious, boastful, proud, rude, selfish, or easily provoked. It does not rejoice in wrongdoing but rejoices in truth, bearing, believing, hoping, and enduring all things.

Charity never fails, while prophecy, tongues, and partial knowledge will pass away when completeness comes. Paul compares present understanding with childhood and with seeing dimly through a glass; fuller knowledge will be like seeing face to face. Faith, hope, and charity remain, but charity is the greatest. The chapter sets enduring love above impressive abilities or outward accomplishments.

chapters.title: Spiritual gifts must build up an orderly church

parts.text: Paul urges pursuit of charity and gifts that strengthen the church, especially prophecy. Uninterpreted tongues do not instruct listeners, while understandable speech comforts and builds them up. Prayer and singing should involve understanding as well as spirit. He prefers a few intelligible words in church to thousands in an unknown tongue. Prophecy can expose an unbeliever’s heart and lead him to acknowledge God’s presence.

Gatherings must aim at mutual edification. Tongues require interpretation and orderly turns; without an interpreter the speaker must remain silent in church. Prophets likewise speak in turn and their messages are judged. God is the author of peace, not confusion. Paul directs women to silence in the churches and learning from husbands at home, and concludes that everything must be done decently and in order.

chapters.title: Christ’s resurrection guarantees victory over death

parts.text: Paul recalls the gospel: Christ died for sins, was buried, and rose the third day according to Scripture, appearing to many witnesses and finally Paul. Denying resurrection makes faith empty and leaves sins unforgiven. But Christ is risen, the firstfruits, followed by those belonging to him at his coming. He reigns until every enemy, including death, is destroyed, then delivers the kingdom to the Father. Resurrection gives purpose to faithful endurance.

Using seeds and differing bodies as illustrations, Paul explains resurrection from corruption, weakness, and dishonour into incorruption, power, and glory. Believers will bear the heavenly image. Not all will die, but all will be changed at the last trump as the dead rise incorruptible. God gives victory through Christ, making steadfast labour in the Lord worthwhile.

chapters.title: A collection, travel plans, and final exhortations

parts.text: Paul directs each believer to set aside a weekly contribution according to prosperity for the saints, with approved representatives carrying it to Jerusalem. He hopes to visit Corinth after travelling through Macedonia, perhaps staying through winter. For now he remains in Ephesus, where opportunity and opposition are both great. Timotheus should be welcomed without fear; Apollos will visit when he has opportunity.

The Corinthians must watch, stand firmly in faith, be strong, and do everything with charity. Paul commends Stephanas’s household and other workers who refresh the saints, urging recognition of their service. Churches and fellow believers send greetings. He closes in his own hand with a solemn warning concerning failure to love Christ, followed by grace and his love for them all.
